subject: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification - follow-up (ACME)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T15:02:00Z
Subject: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification - follow-up (ACME)

Hi John / ACME network team,

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on performance qualification for Redwood Private in your VPC: 

Key SLOs you confirmed on the call:
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for inference responses (cold start excluded).
- Streaming requirement: server-sent events (SSE) or chunked HTTP streaming with sub-50ms token cadence preferred for interactive use cases.
- Throughput: baseline 500 requests/sec with burst to 1k for short durations.
- Concurrency: sustained 50 concurrent inference sessions.

Network / deployment constraints we discussed:
- You plan to peer our service via VPC Peering / Transit Gateway (AWS).
- Egress controls: traffic must originate from our designated Redwood IP ranges; ACME firewall rules are managed by NetOps.
- Internal latency budget: you aim for <20ms intra-VPC RTT to avoid exceeding the p95 target after processing.

Requested items for lab qualification (next steps):
1) ACME to confirm preferred connectivity method (VPC Peering vs Transit Gateway) and provide a contact for finalizing peering/VPN schedule.
2) ACME to confirm any firewall rules or proxy that would terminate TLS or perform deep packet inspection (DPI). DPI can add variable latency; we need to validate with test traffic.
3) ACME to provide a short-term test window (2-4 hours) where we can run a load test from a Redwood staging cluster into your environment. Proposed windows below.
4) Credit/telemetry: we will run a short test harness that produces token-level logs and p95/p99 metrics. ACME to confirm which metrics we can send to the shared S3 bucket or a presigned URL.

Proposed test windows (PST):
- Tue Oct 13, 09:00-12:00
- Wed Oct 14, 13:00-16:00

I've attached a short test plan and checklist for your NetOps team. If these SLOs look off, call them out now — otherwise we'll schedule the lab test once you confirm connectivity and the firewall details.

Attachments: redwood-test-plan.md (test steps), redwood-private-network-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>

Cc: ACME Network Ops <netops@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC network qualification - follow-up (ACME)

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the test plan. Quick answers from NetOps after syncing: 

- Connectivity: ACME prefers Transit Gateway for central routing. We can establish a peering attachment to Redwood's account or terminate a site-to-site VPN if you prefer. Either is fine; TGW preferred for future multi-account scaling.
- Firewall / proxies: We have an outbound proxy cluster in front of egress and a perimeter firewall. The proxy does TLS passthrough for the ports you use today, but we have inline IDS that may inspect headers for large payloads. IDS adds nondeterministic latency spikes (~5-25ms) depending on inspection rules.
- MTU: default 1500, but our VPNs often use 1420 when IPSec is in the path.
- Ports: We allow 443/ TLS, and can open specific port ranges if needed.

Questions from our side:
1) Can Redwood provide a small sample load script and the exact IP ranges we should allow?
2) For streaming SSE, does Redwood keep a long-lived TCP connection per session? If so, do you multiplex many sessions per connection or create one connection per client session?
3) What telemetry do you need in the S3 bucket? We'll need to confirm access patterns and retention.

We can commit to a test window on Oct 14th, 13:00-16:00 PST. If you need the 13th morning window, say so and we'll try to free some team capacity.

--
John Doe
Senior Network Engineer, ACME Corp
j.doe@acme.com
netops@acme.com

Thanks John — great context and really helpful. Short answers inline and next steps: 

- Load script / IPs: I attached a small sample load script as part of the test plan; the staging harness will run from our AWS staging account. IP ranges to allow: 3.12.45.0/24, 52.120.0.0/18, and 34.210.128.0/17 (these are our staging egress ranges for the lab; we'll provide final ranges for production peering).
- Streaming / connections: Redwood will open one long-lived TCP/TLS connection per client session for streaming SSE. We can also proxy-multiplex multiple logical sessions per connection if you prefer to keep connection counts low — let us know which is easier for your proxy. For the lab we can run one-connection-per-session to validate worst-case resource usage.
- Telemetry: we'll push a gzipped CSV of token-level timing samples and aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99, error rates) to a presigned S3 URL you provide. Retention: we keep test artifacts for 7 days unless you request otherwise.

Proposed next steps and responsibilities:
1) ACME NetOps: confirm TGW attachment or VPN and open the three staging IP ranges above (or confirm alternate egress IPs). Confirm MTU for the test path.
2) Redwood (Jordan + Infra): provision staging cluster and run initial smoke tests in the morning of Oct 14. Jordan, please coordinate.
3) Joint test: Oct 14 13:00-16:00 PST. We'll start with a low-rate ramp to 500 rps, validate p95 latency, then run short bursts to 1k rps.

Attachment: redwood-test-plan.md (includes load script sample)

If TGW is the final path, happy to loop in our infra eng for peering ACL review.

Best,
Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: ACME lab test & infra action items (deal ACME-2026-Q4-EXPAND)

Folks — internal summary / action items after ACME confirmed Oct 14 test window: 

Summary:
- ACME (John + NetOps) prefers Transit Gateway attachment and can open firewall rules for our staging egress ranges. They called out possible IDS-induced jitter (5-25ms).
- Confirmed SLO target: p95 <= 200ms; streaming via SSE; baseline 500 rps / burst to 1k; concurrency 50.

Action items:
- Jordan: provision a Redwood staging cluster in us-west-2 with identical runtime config to our Private builds. Attach ephemeral egress ranges: 3.12.45.0/24, 52.120.0.0/18, 34.210.128.0/17. Please enable detailed timing telemetry and token-level sampling in the runner. (Due: 2026-10-13 12:00 UTC)
- Jordan: prepare load script and smoke-run config (script included in redwood-test-plan.md). Validate SSE connection handling under 50 concurrent sessions. (Due: 2026-10-13 12:00 UTC)
- Laura: route this to Infra/Networking for peering ACL review and help triage any MTU/IPSec settings if ACME opts for VPN instead of TGW.
- Marissa: coordinate the presigned S3 URL with ACME and own the test window communication.

Risks to call out:
- ACME IDS could add variable latency spikes that push p95 above target; we should capture p99 and jitter histograms so we can propose mitigation (bypass inspection for peered traffic, or route via a dedicated path).
- If ACME uses 1420 MTU via IPSec, we may see larger TCP segmentation overhead — mark for validation.

I'll update the HubSpot record (ID: 123456) and INF-3210 with results.

Thanks — Marissa
